key_insight: PARA-PV improves photovoltaic forecasting by combining physics-aware retrieval, a frozen foundation-model prior, and distribution-shift correction to better handle weather, day-night transitions, and regime changes.
engineering_relevance: The method can support more reliable grid dispatch and renewable integration by producing forecasts that respect PV operating physics while adapting to changing conditions.
method: Retrieves historical patches and analogous trajectories matched by temporal shape, power level, PV state, and intra-day period to build a physically grounded base forecast.
Uses a frozen Chronos foundation model with a lightweight residual adapter to inject broad temporal priors without overriding PV-specific behavior.
Applies physics-aware distribution-shift correction plus a regime-weighted loss to handle peak, ramping, night-time, and regular conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a PV forecasting framework evaluated for accuracy under weather variability and regime shifts, with a publicly available code release for reproducibility.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of historical retrieval and the correctness of the shift-correction gates, which could be sensitive to site-specific data and missing weather/operating signals.
paper_title: PARA-PV: Physics-Aware Retrieval-Augmented PV Prediction Based on Frozen Foundation Model and Distribution Shift Correction
